newsitem.title: GERMANY: North Koreans living on 100 gram ration - diplomat.
newsitem.headline: North Koreans living on 100 gram ration - diplomat.

text.p: Famine-threatened North Koreans are living on a basic ration of 100 grams per day and food is being distributed under a system similar to one used in wartime, a North Korean diplomat was quoted as saying.

Ri Sang-yu, a counsellor in the Office for the Protection of North Korean Interests in Berlin, was quoted in Saturday's edition of the Neues Deutschland daily as saying North Korea had suffered "enormous" economic and food shortages.
But he said the situation was not as bad as it was being depicted in the Western press.

"The ration is 100 grams per person per day until the next harvest. But there are supplements for people undertaking heavy physical work. We have built up the sort of distribution system like the one we knew during wartime," he said.
He said all citizens were registered at distribution points, which provided them with rations according to the number of people in their household.
Ri also accused "right-wing conservative American forces, Japanese reactionaries and South Korean puppets" of spreading lies about the situation in North Korea.
"The Western media are reporting hundreds of deaths from hunger. This is not correct. The situation is difficult but not as it is being protrayed by Western media," he said.
"The losses in terms of the economy and in terms of food are enormous but the North Korean people are full of optimism and confidence in the future."
